title: Microsoft 365 Backup: Teams channel backup and recovery
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap scope and dates match, and the existing backup controls and prices are supported by Microsoft documentation. Teams-specific pricing, roles and configuration remain unpublished; minor corrections should complete the abbreviated control paths and name the Graph request property.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup currently protects OneDrive accounts, SharePoint sites and Exchange mailboxes.
claims.quote: With the ability to back up all or select SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, Exchange mailboxes, and Entra directory objects

claims.claim: Existing OneDrive, SharePoint and Exchange backups have frequent restore points.
claims.quote: | Full OneDrive account and full SharePoint site restore | 10 minutes | One week, through the configured recovery window of up to 10 years |

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup provides fast restores for its existing workloads.
claims.quote: Fast restore (see performance expectations later in this article).

claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 Backup recovery is available through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: This is what the Microsoft 365 Backup product offers, both through the Microsoft 365 admin center, and via partner applications built on the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage platform.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the Teams backup default on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel backup pricing rate default enable backup policies roles restore destinations 570668; Teams Backup default roles restore. Opened backup-setup, backup-overview and backup-view-edit-policies; no Teams default or existing-policy coverage is stated.

claims.claim: Purview retention preserves compliance copies of Teams messages.
claims.quote: If a chat or channel message is edited or deleted by a user during the retention period, the original message is copied (if edited) or moved (if deleted) to the SubstrateHolds folder.

claims.claim: Retained Teams message copies are searchable through eDiscovery.
claims.quote: Messages stored in mailboxes, including the hidden folders, are searchable by eDiscovery tools. Until messages are permanently deleted from the SubstrateHolds folder, they remain searchable by eDiscovery tools.

claims.claim: Deleted teams can be restored within 30 days after deletion.
claims.quote: Deleted teams can be restored within 30 days after deletion.

claims.claim: Deleted shared channels can be restored within 30 days after deletion.
claims.quote: Deleted shared channel can be restored within 30 days after deletion.

claims.claim: Backup restores can bring back deliberately deleted content.
claims.quote: Full Exchange mailbox item restores or granular item restores using search, for modified or fully deleted items.

claims.claim: Backup data remains within the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary.
claims.quote: Data never leaves the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary and honors the geographic locations of your current data residency. Limited metadata (for example, tenantID and siteIDs) sent to Azure for billing purposes only.

claims.claim: Backup data respects the tenant's geographic residency.
claims.quote: Data never leaves the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary and honors the geographic locations of your current data residency.

claims.claim: Multi-geo backup is supported for existing workloads.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup supports the backup of sites and user accounts from both the central and satellite locations.

claims.claim: Teams backup and restore role mappings are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Teams channel backup pricing rate default enable backup policies roles restore destinations 570668; Teams Backup default roles restore. Opened backup-setup and backup-overview; the role matrix has OneDrive, SharePoint, Exchange and Entra, not Teams.

claims.claim: The existing backup role matrix documents OneDrive, SharePoint and Exchange privileges.
claims.quote: | Admin role | OneDrive | SharePoint | Exchange | Entra |

claims.claim: With departmental billing enabled, creating and editing backup policies requires Owner or Contributor access to the applicable Azure subscription.
claims.quote: every backup admin should also have an Owner or Contributor role on the subscription. This way only an approved admin who is given spending power on a subscription can create and edit backups

claims.claim: Departmental billing is not described as restricting all restore authority.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup departmental billing restrict restore authority permissions Owner Contributor. Opened backup-billing and backup-setup; the restriction describes creation and update of policies, not all restore authority.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go is the entry to the new Backup billing setup experience.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center, and then go to Billing > Pay-as-you-go. On the Billing policies tab, select Add a billing policy.
claims.fix: In Cost and licensing, give the setup route as 'Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > Add a billing policy', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-billing-node. The checklist can retain its entry-point wording.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The new pay-as-you-go experience supports departmental billing for Backup.
claims.quote: You can connect more than one billing policies to Microsoft 365 Backup in the Billing Policies tab in Pay-as-you-go page.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The new pay-as-you-go billing experience offers budget alerts.
claims.quote: To send budget spending alerts, in the Recipients box, select the name of one or more groups that you want to receive alert messages.

claims.claim: An Azure subscription can be created during billing-policy setup in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: From the Subscription drop-down list, select an existing Azure subscription, or select Create a new subscription.

claims.claim: Backup customers onboarded before April 2026 can migrate their billing management to the new experience.
claims.quote: Existing customers who onboarded to Backup before April 1, 2026 who are interested in splitting Microsoft 365 Backup consumption into multiple Azure subscriptions can now migrate their billing management from Setup tab

claims.claim: The Backup setup guide names SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator for admin-center access and Backup setup.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator is a dedicated role for the tool.
claims.quote: We have also introduced a new dedicated role for this tool, the Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup in the Microsoft 365 admin center reaches the page for workload backup policies and restore points.
claims.quote: Select Settings. Select Microsoft 365 Backup from the list of products. On the Microsoft 365 Backup page, in the SharePoint section, select Set up policy.
claims.fix: Keep the existing route but add to the first row's note: 'For SharePoint policy creation, continue under SharePoint to Set up policy.' The complete entry route is 'Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > SharePoint > Set up policy'; the remaining wizard steps are on https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-view-edit-policies#create-backup-policies.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row and prose
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/solutions/backupRestore/sharePointProtectionPolicies creates a SharePoint protection policy, not a Teams policy.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/solutions/backupRestore/sharePointProtectionPolicies
siteProtectionUnits | siteProtectionUnit collection | Collection of the siteProtectionUnits to be added to the sharePointProtectionPolicy object. Required.
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[0].note and the rendered note: 'The request body sets siteProtectionUnits; the policy is created inactive.' These properties and state are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/backuprestoreroot-post-sharepointprotectionpolicies?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first table row

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > Add a billing policy starts billing-policy and budget-alert setup in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote:
On the Billing policies tab, select Add a billing policy.
On the Budget page, if you want to set a budget, select the Set a budget for this policy checkbox.
claims.fix: Keep controls[1].ui.path for creating the policy. Add this row note and render it: 'To configure alerts on an existing policy, use Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > policy > Budget > Settings > Set a budget for this policy, then configure Send email alerts.' This route is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-billing-node#add-a-budget-to-an-existing-billing-policy.
